description: Start a batch of checks: send `selection` (contact ids, or every contact that matches filters), or `campaignId` for a campaign's leads that haven't had its first email yet. With `campaignId`, `leads: unchecked` (the default) takes the leads with no verdict, one out of date, or a check that got no answer; `leads: needs_review` checks the risky and unknown ones again. Up to 50,000 contacts a batch. It answers at once: follow the batch with get_email_check_run, or wait for the email_check.run_completed event. The email_check.run_held event says when the batch waits on hold. A verdict stays good 30 days, and an address that already has one is not checked again. `recheck: true` checks it anyway, but never buys a new answer from the checking service less than 24 hours after the last one. Pass an `intentKey` so a retry answers the same batch. Each address a checking service answers, ours or the paid one, counts once against your plan's checks for the month; a retry after the paid service failed counts again. When none are left (a plan with no monthly limit never runs out) it answers 429 serverErrors.quotaAddressChecks, with `details.resetAt` (the 1st, 00:00 UTC) and `details.upgradeTo`. It does so whenever the call would queue a check, even one we would then answer for free, without the checking service. While the workspace's last payment has failed, the same call answers 402 serverErrors.checksPaymentFailed and queues nothing, until the workspace owner updates the card (get_billing; a manage_billing handoff asks them). At most 30 of these calls a minute per workspace.

campaignId.description: Check this campaign's leads that haven't had its first email yet, instead of a selection.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.

intentKey.description: Your own name for this batch, up to 255 characters. Send the same intentKey with the same contacts and settings again and you get the same batch back, never a second one, for as long as the batch is kept: 30 days after it finishes. The same intentKey with different settings or contacts answers 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED: send a new one. Names starting with import: or launch: are refused.

leads.description: With campaignId: unchecked (the default) checks the leads with no verdict of ours, one out of date, or a check that got no answer. needs_review checks the leads whose fresh verdict is risky or unknown again.

recheck.description: Check again even when the verdict is still fresh. A verdict the checking service gave in the last 24 hours comes back as it is, with no new check.

expectedCount.description: How many contacts you expect this to touch: the count you showed or checked (count_contacts, minus the ones in exclude). If the contacts that match changed since, nothing happens and it answers 409 serverErrors.selectionChanged, with the number that match now in params.count.

check.description: Only contacts whose address check is at this point. valid, risky, unknown: a fresh verdict of ours. invalid: the address can't receive mail. not_checked: we never checked it (an imported verdict that isn't invalid counts as not checked). checking: a check is under way. waiting: a check is on hold. needs_retry: no answer came back, so check it again. out_of_date: our verdict is too old.

segmentId.description: Only contacts in this segment (list_segments): whoever matches its conditions now. It combines with the other filters. A segment that was deleted answers 404.

name: start_email_checks
title: Check many addresses
